name: invite-and-enter
scope: Owns `open`, `invite`, `enter` and `own-layer-made` of "The client's contract", with "Rules for every call" as it applies to them; it starts the module of "What Auth is", placed as "Where it goes" says. The hard part it isolates is the agreement of an account, a claim and a person when writes race: the paragraph of **enter.** that begins "What must hold", and "A claim names one person for good" and "A person has one claim" of **invite.**, under "No one task that everything passes through". Its operations are also bound by **invite.** and **enter.** of "What each write does", with the paragraph that begins "`:own-layer` and `:making` are how a break between Auth and the store is met"; the first bullet of "What takes a thing out of what is live", which says how take-outs apply to them; in "What the runtime does, and Auth does not check", its first bullet, the bullet on two refusals that apply to one write, and the bullet on a provider's name and `:own-layer`; "What can be erased later"; "Not in this build"; and the bullets of "What must hold at full life" that bear on them. State it must figure out: the invitations and their claims; the links of accounts to persons, with what the provider said; the events of these writes; and the record of a person who has entered, with her own layer, her `:making` and the flag that `own-layer-made` sets. Everything in that state and in those events that names a human being is bound by "What can be erased later" and by the last paragraph of "What Auth is". The record of a person who has entered is this stage's interface to every later stage: it must make achievable what the later writes need of a person as an actor and her own root ("Actor" in "Words"; **begin-sign-in.**, **make-actor.**, **end-actor.**, **ask, answer-ask.**), and the `:own-layer` and `:own-layer-made?` of `who-is` under "`who-is` is the read of every request".

name: standing-under-a-root
scope: Owns `make-actor`, `end-actor`, `begin-sign-in`, `replace-secret`, `end-sign-in`, `open-session`, `close-session`, `who-is` and `under` of "The client's contract", with "Rules for every call" as it applies to them. The hard part it isolates is what is live under a root and what takes it out, at full life: "Standing" in "Words"; the whole of "What takes a thing out of what is live"; and the cascade of **end-actor.** with the bound of **make-actor.** ("no read costs more with the depth"). Its operations are also bound by their paragraphs of "What each write does"; the repeat rule of "Rules for every call"; in "What the runtime does, and Auth does not check", its first bullet, the bullet on two refusals that apply to one write and a session's `:in-use`, and the bullet that begins "The numbers that the plan sizes" as it bears on `who-is` and `open-session`; and every bullet of "What must hold at full life" as it bears on the actors, sign-ins and sessions of one root. It reads the first stage's record of a person who has entered, and `who-is` gives that record's `:own-layer` and `:own-layer-made?` under "`who-is` is the read of every request". State it must figure out: the actors of each root and who made whom; the sign-ins and sessions with their facts, readable after they end ("Nothing is deleted") and bound by the last paragraph of "What Auth is"; what is live under each root, kept apart from that history ("What is watched and what is read on each request is kept apart from that history"); the events of these writes, decided as "Order" says; and what lets each write that names a `:root` take out what has passed. This state is the interface to the two later stages and must make their requirements achievable: the yes and the no of **ask, answer-ask.**, with the first bullet of "What takes a thing out of what is live" as it applies to `answer-ask`; and the value of `watch-root`, bound by the paragraph that begins "`watch-root` calls `f`", by "What a runtime watches for one root stays small" and by "How many roots can be watched".

name: ask-and-answer
scope: Owns `ask`, `answer-ask` and `ask-of` of "The client's contract", with "Rules for every call" as it applies to them. The hard part it isolates is an answer that touches an ask ("Ask" in "Words") and a root at once: "The first answer stands"; "Two persons who answer one ask at the same moment"; the refusals of `answer-ask` in the order that the bullet on two refusals that apply to one write sets ("What the runtime does, and Auth does not check"); the first bullet of "What takes a thing out of what is live" as it applies to `answer-ask`; and "A write returns when its effect can be read by any copy of the runtime" for a yes, whose effects are both the ask's and the root's. Its operations are also bound by **ask, answer-ask.** of "What each write does"; the repeat rule of "Rules for every call"; the bullet of "What takes a thing out of what is live" that begins "A time's edge"; the first bullet of "What the runtime does, and Auth does not check"; and the bullets of "What must hold at full life" that bear on asks and answers. State it must figure out: the asks and their answers, and the events of these writes, bound by "A code is bound for good", "Nothing is deleted" and "Scale". On the root's side a yes and a no use the state of the two earlier stages (the record of a person who has entered; the actors, sign-ins, sessions and take-outs of `standing-under-a-root`), which a yes changes as **ask, answer-ask.** says.

name: watch-and-close
scope: Owns `watch-root` and `close!` of "The client's contract", with "Rules for every call" as it applies to them; `close!` is here, in the last stage, because it touches every call of every stage (the word `:closed` in "Rules for every call") and every watch. The hard part it isolates is watching what is live under a root at full life: the paragraph that begins "`watch-root` calls `f`", with its `:softland.auth.client/not-reached`; "What a runtime watches for one root stays small"; "How many roots can be watched", with what the module sets at launch and what the build measures; the figure of watched roots in the bullet of "What the runtime does, and Auth does not check" that begins "The numbers that the plan sizes"; the bullet there on "`watch-root` on a closed client"; and "No one task that everything passes through" as it bears on a watch. It watches the state of what is live under a root that `standing-under-a-root` writes, which the writes of `standing-under-a-root` and `ask-and-answer` change. State it must figure out: what the module sets at launch for "How many roots can be watched".
